overlap_rationale: Both full texts are accessible and share the exact same Swiss empirical case study while differing in overall geographical scope. Study A (International Journal of the Commons, 2023) focuses exclusively on rural water cooperatives in the Canton of Lucerne, Switzerland, detailing a proposed merger/interconnection of three water schemes (S, K, and N) based on participant observation by the lead author at the cantonal department LAWA (February 2021–June 2022) and a private engineering consultancy (from July 2022), alongside 17 semi-structured interviews and archival research. Study B (Water, 2023) explicitly draws on three earlier case studies—citing Study A as Reference [74] alongside two South African studies [75, 76]—to compare three Rooted Water Collectives: two in Limpopo Province, South Africa (Tshakuma and Ga-Moela; fieldwork April 2017–June 2018 plus a 2023 visit) and one in Entlebuch, Canton of Lucerne, Switzerland. The Swiss case in Study B (Section 5.3) is Scheme S from Study A (built in 1962, serving 14 households and a collective cheese factory, undergoing the exact same proposed three-scheme interconnection), relies on the identical February 2021–June 2022 and July 2022+ fieldwork, and reproduces the exact same schematic map (Figure 1 in Study A = Figure 4 in Study B). Thus, the Swiss subsample of Study B directly overlaps with Study A, whereas Study B adds two distinct South African community cases and Study A provides deeper multi-scheme detail on Swiss Cooperatives K and N.
study_a_sample_and_data: Qualitative action-research/participant-observation case study in a rural municipality in the foothills of the Alps, Canton of Lucerne, Switzerland, examining cantonal water-subsidy governance and a project to interconnect three cooperative rural water schemes: Scheme S (built 1962, 14 households and 1 cheese factory), Scheme K (built 1967, 11 households), and Scheme N (reservoirs built 1970). Data collected via participant observation by the first author while employed at the cantonal department for agriculture and forestry (LAWA, Feb 2021–June 2022) and the planning engineering firm (from July 2022), 17 semi-structured interviews (6 current/former government officials, 5 scheme officials, 3 engineers, 2 local politicians, 1 contractor), and cantonal historical/newspaper archives.
study_b_sample_and_data: Comparative qualitative action-research synthesis across three Rooted Water Collectives (RWCs) in two countries: (1) Tshakuma (Muhovhoya section, 113-household user-built scheme in a village of >4,000 households; IWMI 2017 survey N=250), Vhembe District, Limpopo, South Africa; (2) Ga-Moela (~100-household village, Sections A and B reticulations; IWMI 2017 survey N=65), Sekhukhune District, Limpopo, South Africa; and (3) Entlebuch (Scheme S, built 1962, 14 households and a collective cheese facility), Canton of Lucerne, Switzerland. Draws on earlier fieldwork from April 2017–June 2018 and a 2023 revisit in South Africa, plus the exact same Swiss fieldwork (Feb 2021–June 2022 at the cantonal department and July 2022–present at the engineering consultancy), pooling 128 semi-structured interviews across all three cases (28 department officials, 12 scheme officials, 9 engineering consultants, 12 politicians, 3 academics, 64 water users).
